quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Position your vehicle so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
Stop at the stop sign or signal, then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and honk your horn to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Position your vehicle so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move into a position where other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: You may drive faster than the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may ignore no passing zone markings if you started the pass in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: Always stay within the posted speed limit when passing. Only pass in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, which is NOT something you should do?

options.text: Ride at slower speeds than usual.
Leave more distance to stop than usual.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a passenger will handle differently because of the extra weight. Ride slower and allow more stopping distance. The passenger should hold firmly onto the passenger handgrips or the operator's waist—not just the back of the bike.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake gives you the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes together every time you stop.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes.
It is acceptable for a motorcyclist to weave between lanes.
A motorcyclist should ride straight between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcyclist should not weave between lanes.
questions.explanation: Riding between stopped or slow-moving vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to be safe.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on your motorcycle, what tire adjustment might you need to make?

options.text: Reduce the tire pressure.
Make no changes to tire pressure.
Increase the tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase the tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. You will likely need to add a few pounds of pressure to your tires. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat can cushion the impact.
Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle and must ride over it, slow down and approach it at as close to a 90-degree angle as possible.

questions.question: What do convex mirrors do?

options.text: They provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
They provide a wide view of the road behind you.
They are illegal.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to convex mirrors on your motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the maximum engine displacement for a moped?

options.text: 10 cubic centimeters
20 cubic centimeters
50 cubic centimeters

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 cubic centimeters
questions.explanation: Under South Dakota law, a moped may have an engine no larger than 50 cubic centimeters.

questions.question: What is a main cause of single-vehicle motorcycle crashes?

options.text: Riding too fast for weather conditions.
Taking curves too wide.
Running off the road to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking curves too wide.
questions.explanation: A main cause of single-vehicle crashes is motorcyclists taking curves too wide. This can cause the motorcycle to leave the road or hit an object.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield
Slow-moving vehicle
Railroad crossing

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is put on the back of slow-moving vehicles. These vehicles go slower than 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action first, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action first, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can make your motorcycle fall over.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to directional changes:

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to the motorcycle. The added weight makes the motorcycle respond more slowly to your movements. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They warn drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns of a divided roadway ahead.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be traveled upon if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually gives good traction, unless it is raining.
Should be avoided at all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives good traction, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The oily center strip usually provides enough traction for safe riding, except in rain. The strip is usually about two feet wide. Riders can ride on either side of the strip and stay in the center of the lane.

questions.question: It is most important to flash your brake light when:

options.text: Someone is following you too closely.
You will be slowing down suddenly.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are not as noticeable as car brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing or stopping so others notice you are slowing down. This is especially important when you slow down faster than expected.

questions.question: Service signs are:

options.text: Orange with black letters.
Blue with white letters.
Green with white letters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. Services include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your fingers on the clutch and brake levers.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your fingers ready on the clutch and both brakes to reduce your reaction time.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
Inexperienced riders should be in the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front of the group, behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the less experienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: No parking is permitted.
The right edge of a traffic lane.
Traffic must merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: Small vehicles look ________ and slower than they really are.

options.text: Closer
Farther away
Larger

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther away
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge the speed and distance of small vehicles like motorcycles. Do not assume that drivers of larger vehicles can accurately see your speed and location.

questions.question: When riding over rough pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to see the road surface changes.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay on the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: When riding over rough pavement in a work zone, keep your head and eyes up. Ride slowly, keep a steady throttle, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, ride in:

options.text: A single-file line.
Pairs.
A staggered line.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file line.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered line. Switch to a single-file line when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Must go faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must complete passing within the posted speed limit. Only pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on good pavement, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and quickly apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and travels straight.
